intro: Making an appointment, talking to the doctor and understanding tests, prescriptions and sick leave.
p.pedir cita.consejo: It is the usual expression in Spain: «pedir cita» with the doctor. Then you say «tengo cita» on Tuesday.
p.centro de salud.consejo: In Spain it is the first place you go if you are ill. «Salud» has the stress at the end: sa-LUD.
p.consulta.consejo: It is also the visit: «la consulta dura diez minutos». It comes from «consultar».
p.análisis de sangre.consejo: «Análisis» does not change in the plural: «un análisis», «unos análisis». The accent goes on the second a.
p.receta.consejo: It is also a cooking recipe. The context tells you: «la receta del médico», «la receta de la tortilla».
p.estar de baja.consejo: The doctor «da la baja»; you «estás de baja». When you go back, they «dan el alta».
p.mareado.consejo: It comes from «mar»: a ship's movement makes you dizzy. It changes with gender: «mareada».
p.urgencias.consejo: It is almost always plural: «voy a urgencias». It is for serious cases, not for a normal visit.
p.en ayunas.consejo: It is only used in the plural: «en ayunas». Before some tests you have to go like this.
p.especialista.consejo: It works for a man and a woman: «el especialista», «la especialista». It ends in -ista, like «dentista».
p.ingresar.consejo: It also means putting money in the bank. In hospital: «lo ingresaron ayer».
p.vacuna.consejo: The v sounds like b: ba-KU-na. You say «ponerse una vacuna» or «vacunarse».
p.encontrarse mal.consejo: Here «encontrarse» does not mean «to find»: «me encuentro mal» is «me siento mal». The opposite: «me encuentro bien».
p.dar el alta.consejo: It can mean leaving hospital or going back to work. The opposite, for work, is «la baja».
b1.titulo: Going to the doctor in Spain
b1.texto:
In Spain, to see a doctor you first call your **centro de salud** and **pides cita**. The family doctor sees you in the **consulta**; if needed, they send you to a **especialista**.

The doctor may ask for an **análisis de sangre** (sometimes you must go **en ayunas**, without eating) or give you a **receta** for the pharmacy.

If you cannot work because you are ill, the doctor gives you the **baja**: **estás de baja**. When you recover, they **dan el alta**.

If it is serious, you go to **urgencias**, and sometimes you are **ingresado** in hospital. In other countries the system is different.
b2.f0.texto: I would like to make an appointment with my doctor.
b2.f1.texto: For when do you want it?
b2.f2.texto: I have been dizzy for three days.
b2.f3.texto: Doctor Ruiz will see you tomorrow at ten.
b2.f4.texto: And can she give me sick leave?
b2.f5.texto: The doctor decides whether you need sick leave.
b2.f6.texto: Perhaps she will ask you for a blood test.
b2.f7.texto: Do I have to go fasting?
b2.f8.texto: She will tell you if it is necessary.
b4.texto:
At reception and with the doctor you use **usted**:

- **Quería** pedir cita. (the imperfect softens the wish and is more polite than «quiero»)
- **Vaya** a urgencias. · **Póngase** en contacto con nosotros. (command with «usted»)
- La doctora **le dirá** si hace falta. (the future announces what will happen)

With «usted», the pronoun is **le**, **lo** or **la**, not «te».
b4.e0.texto: I would like to make an appointment for tomorrow.
b4.e2.texto: The doctor will tell you the result of the test.
b5.f0.texto: The waiting room smells of cleanliness and chamomile.
b5.f1.texto: A white light falls from the ceiling onto the plastic chairs.
b5.f2.texto: Mario waits with a crumpled piece of paper between his fingers.
b5.f3.texto: On the wall, a round clock counts the minutes with a tired tick-tock.
b5.f4.texto: A little girl draws a crooked house in a notebook.
b5.f5.texto: The door of the consulting room opens slowly.
b5.f6.texto: Doctor Ruiz welcomes Mario with a calm smile.
b5.f7.texto: She takes his blood pressure with a device that makes a soft hum.
b5.f8.texto: Mario describes his dizzy spells in a low voice.
b5.f9.texto: On leaving, Mario carries in his hand a prescription and an appointment for the blood test.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! In Spain you say «pedir cita» with the doctor.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Dar cita» is what the health centre does. The person calling asks for it.
b6.o2.refuerzo: With «cita» you do not say «tomar». You use «pedir».
b6.pregunta: You want to book with the doctor. Which verb is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! The baja is the medical permission not to work.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is something else: the baja is about work, not about the emergency room.
b7.o2.refuerzo: A vaccine is a medicine. The baja is a permission.
b7.pregunta: The doctor gives you the «baja». What does it mean?
b8.frase: Tengo cita con la médica mañana a las diez
b8.traduccion: I have an appointment with the doctor tomorrow at ten
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Ve» is the command for «tú». With «usted» you say «vaya».
b9.o1.refuerzo: That's it! «Vaya» is the command with «usted».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Va» is present: it tells something, it does not give an order.
b9.pregunta: You speak with «usted». Which form is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «De baja» means not working due to illness. It is not about eating.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Ingresado» means being in hospital. It is not about eating.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Yes! «En ayunas» means without having eaten or drunk anything.
b10.pregunta: Before the test you cannot eat. How must you go?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I have an appointment tomorrow.»
b12.o0: Tiene que quedarse en el hospital
b12.o0.refuerzo: That is the opposite: staying is «estar ingresado».
b12.o1: Ya está recuperado y puede irse
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The alta says the patient can now leave or go back to work.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is «estar de baja». The alta is the opposite.
b12.pregunta: «Le han dado el alta». What does it mean?
p.doctora.consejo: Feminine of «doctor». It is used as a title: «la doctora Ruiz».
p.decide.consejo: Form of «decidir». The c before i sounds th: de-THI-de.
p.necesita.consejo: Form of «necesitar». The c before e and i sounds th: ne-the-SI-ta.
p.pida.consejo: Subjunctive of «pedir». After «quizá» it expresses doubt: «quizá le pida un análisis».
p.dirá.consejo: Future of «decir». It is irregular: «diré», «dirás», «dirá». The accent shows the stress.
p.cita.consejo: The c before i sounds th: THI-ta. «Pedir cita» and «tener cita» are the usual phrases.
p.análisis.consejo: The accent is on the second a: a-NA-li-sis. It does not change in the plural: «los análisis».
p.techo.consejo: The ch sounds as in «chocolate»: TE-cho. It is masculine: «el techo».
p.sillas.consejo: The ll sounds y: SI-yas. The singular is «la silla».
p.arrugado.consejo: It comes from «arruga», a wrinkle. The rr is strong: a-rru-GA-do.
p.redondo.consejo: The initial r is strong: rre-DON-do. It changes with gender: «redonda».
p.tic.consejo: A sound word: it imitates the clock. Together: «tic tac».
p.tac.consejo: A sound word, second half of «tic tac». The c at the end sounds k.
p.torcida.consejo: Feminine of «torcido», the participle of «torcer». The c before i sounds th.
p.cuaderno.consejo: The «ua» is one syllable and the stress is on «der»: kwa-DER-no.
p.recibe.consejo: Form of «recibir». The initial r is strong and the c before i sounds th: rre-THI-be.
p.toma.consejo: Form of «tomar». «Tomar la tensión» means to measure blood pressure.
p.zumbido.consejo: The z sounds th: thum-BI-do. It comes from «zumbar».
p.mareos.consejo: It comes from «mar»: the movement of a ship makes you dizzy. The singular is «el mareo».
p.enfermedad.consejo: It comes from «enfermo» and ends in -dad, so it is feminine: «la enfermedad».
p.recuperado.consejo: Participle of «recuperar». The initial r is strong: rre-ku-pe-RA-do.
